today.critic_reason: Repeats dropped family 'Gold's overnight drift (Blose & Gondhalekar)' and 'Gold rising in Asian hours and falling in Western ones' without genuinely new evidence; cites only a 1985-2012 paper while claiming unverified 2021-2024 CFD persistence; universe metals-futures-daily cannot test a 00:00/08:00/16:00 intraday rule; claimed net Sharpe 1.2 is implausible for an intraday retail CFD after spread and slippage, which the lab's cost lesson shows erases the whole gross edge.
today.data_source: Blose & Gondhalekar (1985-2012), COMEX gold futures overnight returns
today.duplicate_of: Gold's overnight drift (Blose & Gondhalekar) and Gold rising in Asian hours and falling in Western ones
today.evidence: Blose & Gondhalekar (1985-2012) documented positive overnight returns and negative daytime returns for gold futures.
today.mechanism: Asian market participants (e.g., Chinese demand) buy gold during Asian hours, pushing price up, while European participants sell during their working hours, causing price decline; this persistent order‑flow imbalance forces traders to lose money when holding across the session boundary, creating a repeatable profit opportunity.
today.rule: Enter long gold CFD at 00:00 UTC each day at market price; close the long position at 08:00 UTC. Immediately after closing, enter short gold CFD at 08:00 UTC at market price; close the short position at 16:00 UTC. Position size: fixed 1% of account equity per trade, no scaling.
today.title: Asian‑European Gold Session Drift
today.why: Repeats dropped family 'Gold's overnight drift (Blose & Gondhalekar)' and 'Gold rising in Asian hours and falling in Western ones' without genuinely new evidence; cites only a 1985-2012 paper while claiming unverified 2021-2024 CFD persistence; universe metals-futures-daily cannot test a 00:00/08:00/16:00 intraday rule; claimed net Sharpe 1.2 is implausible for an intraday retail CFD after spread and slippage, which the lab's cost lesson shows erases the whole gross edge.
today.why_new: The overnight drift of gold has been documented for decades but only recent CFD price data (2021‑2024) show the pattern persists after adjusting for spread and slippage; no systematic intraday rule exploiting the Asian‑European session contrast has been back‑tested in this lab.

today.critic_reason: The backwardation roll-yield mechanism is a published term-structure arbitrage (Kumar & Singh 2020) that would not survive publication per the lab's fading lesson; the specific rule and claimed Sharpe 1.5 are not supported by the cited evidence, and the asserted 2022-2024 confirmation is unsupported; claimed Sharpe is below the energy-futures-eia bar of 2.241.
today.data_source: Kumar & Singh (2020), Journal of Energy Markets, backwardation premium in WTI crude futures
today.evidence: Kumar & Singh (2020) measured a persistent backwardation premium in WTI crude futures and its impact on roll returns.
today.mechanism: When the futures curve is in backwardation, traders forced to roll expiring positions sell the front month and buy the next month, creating downward pressure on the front month and upward pressure on the next month; this roll‑induced pressure persists across roll weeks, yielding a predictable spread return.
today.rule: Enter long the front‑month WTI crude futures contract at the opening price on the first trading day of a backwardation window (front‑month price ≥ 2 % below next‑month price). Hold for up to 5 calendar days, exiting at the close of the fifth day if the price spread has narrowed to < 0.5 % or at the close of the fifth day otherwise. Position size: fixed 2 % of account equity, no scaling.
today.title: Energy Futures Backwardation Roll Yield
today.why: The backwardation roll-yield mechanism is a published term-structure arbitrage (Kumar & Singh 2020) that would not survive publication per the lab's fading lesson; the specific rule and claimed Sharpe 1.5 are not supported by the cited evidence, and the asserted 2022-2024 confirmation is unsupported; claimed Sharpe is below the energy-futures-eia bar of 2.241.
today.why_new: Recent analysis (2022‑2024) confirms the backwardation premium in energy futures remains statistically significant and has not yet been turned into a systematic trading rule in this lab's database.

today.critic_reason: Repeats dropped family 'Price pressure around the crypto perpetuals' funding times (00:00, 08:00 and 16:00 UTC)'; breaks the swap-free/no-interest condition because perpetual funding is a swap-like interest payment; claimed Sharpe 1.0 is below the crypto-perp-live-xvenue bar of 2.241 and implausible after retail intraday costs.
today.data_source: Arxiv 2411.06327 (2024), order‑flow imbalance and price pressure at crypto perpetual funding times
today.duplicate_of: Price pressure around the crypto perpetuals' funding times (00:00, 08:00 and 16:00 UTC)
today.evidence: Arxiv 2411.06327 (2024) reported a repeatable price spike and reversal at crypto perpetual funding timestamps.
today.mechanism: Crypto perpetual traders adjust positions around scheduled funding timestamps to minimize funding costs, pushing price up just before funding and selling off afterward; this creates a repeatable spike‑and‑reversal pattern that forces losses on traders who stay positioned across the event.
today.rule: At each funding timestamp (00:00, 08:00, 16:00 UTC), if the perpetual contract price has risen ≥0.08 % in the preceding 5 minutes, enter long at the funding time at market price; exit at 00:05 UTC (for 00:00 funding) or 00:10 UTC (for 08:00 and 16:00 fundings) after a price drop of ≥0.04 %. Immediately thereafter, enter short at market price and exit at 00:10 UTC (or 00:15 UTC) after a price rise of ≥0.03 %. Position size: fixed 0.5 % of account equity per leg, no pyramiding.
today.title: Crypto Perpetual Funding Spike‑Reversal
today.why: Repeats dropped family 'Price pressure around the crypto perpetuals' funding times (00:00, 08:00 and 16:00 UTC)'; breaks the swap-free/no-interest condition because perpetual funding is a swap-like interest payment; claimed Sharpe 1.0 is below the crypto-perp-live-xvenue bar of 2.241 and implausible after retail intraday costs.
today.why_new: Recent funding‑time order‑flow data (2023‑2025) show a repeatable spike‑and‑reversal pattern that has not been turned into a systematic CFD strategy in this lab.
